title: Reading: Ælfric, on the Creation
subtitle: On anginne gesceōp God heofonan and eorþan.
objectives: Understand and apply the concepts of Reading: Ælfric, on the Creation.
Read and parse examples from authentic Old English texts.

sections.heading: Core concept
sections.body:
On anginne gesceōp God heofonan and eorþan. Sēo eorþe sōþlīce wæs īdel and ǣmtig, and þēostru wǣron ofer þǣre nīwelnesse brādnesse, and Godes gāst wæs geferod ofer wæteru.

Translation: 'In the beginning God created heaven and earth. The earth was idle and empty, and darkness was over the breadth of the abyss, and God's spirit was borne over the waters.'

This is Ælfric's translation of Genesis 1:1-2. Ælfric (c. 955–1010) was a Benedictine monk, the greatest prose stylist of late Old English. His homilies and saints' lives are models of clear, rhythmic prose.

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: Ælfric's prose is a model of clarity and rhythm.

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.body: anginne (beginning, dat.), gesceōp (created, past sg.), heofonan (heaven, acc.), eorþan (earth, acc.), sōþlīce (truly), īdel (idle, empty), ǣmtig (empty), þēostru (darkness, nom. pl.), nīwelnesse (abyss, gen.), brādnesse (breadth, gen.), gāst (spirit, nom.), geferod (borne, past part.), wæteru (waters, acc. pl.).
